experiment: Gate 004: Temporal no-reset identifiability under limited interventions
algorithmic_assumptions: exact known spatially local baseline .6 self+.1 four-neighbors
single spatial shift with known positive coefficient .1 or no link
independent additive sensor noise with known absolute variance
agent can inject controlled input before each new transition
primary_conclusion: Breaking a passive exact alias in a continuously evolving unknown-offset simulator makes correct remote address recovery possible; an observation-error correction prevents false remote links in known-R null worlds.
important_negative: Broadband white noise outperformed the candidate-directed Fourier strategy at 2/4/8 actions: 10/32/40 of 40 versus 7/22/39 of 40, while both reached 40/40 after 16. The targeted policy has not demonstrated superiority to white noise.
sensor_noise_ablation: At 16 active steps, corrected null detection was 40/40 for both white and targeted; setting calibrated R falsely to 0 yielded 0/40 for both under identical hidden null physics.
process_caveat: Stochastic process disturbances also excite missing modes in this synthetic world, but process variance changes total latent power; no universal threshold or comparison with Luotain2 fixed-R normalization is claimed.
limitations: Remote coefficient and local stencil supplied
Small synthetic known model family and controlled actions
Sensor error known i.i.d.; correlated/unknown errors untested
No confidence intervals or false discovery bounds for selected candidate
No real data or physically constrained action
Not a novel theorem or proof of a general law of AI
